0.headline: Arcil IPO booked 63% so far on Day 2; GMP drops to 11%
0.heading: Arcil IPO booked 63% so far on Day 2; GMP drops to 11%
0.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Asset Reconstruction Company India (Arcil), backed by Avenue Capital Group and State Bank of India, was subscribed 63 percent as of 12:45 pm on September 10, as per the NSE data.
0.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Asset Reconstruction Company India (Arcil), backed by Avenue Capital Group and State Bank of India, was subscribed 63 percent as of 12:45 pm on September 10, as per the NSE data.

The Rs 733-crore public issue received bids for 2,32,79,348 equity shares against 3,69,12,363 shares available for subscription. Retail investors emerged as the strongest participants, with their portion subscribed 93 percent, while the non-institutional investor category was subscribed 65 percent.

In the grey market, Arcil shares were trading at a premium of 10.79 percent on September 10, according to InvestorGain. The grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of market sentiment and should not be treated as a guaranteed listing gain or return.

Read Also: Steamhouse India IPO subscribed 90% so far on Day 2; GMP at 25%

The IPO comes with a price band of Rs 132-139 per share and will remain open for subscription until September 11. The issue is entirely an offer-for-sale (OFS), meaning Arcil itself will not receive any funds raised through the IPO.

Ahead of the public issue, the company raised Rs 219.89 crore through its anchor book. It allotted 1.58 crore equity shares to 21 institutional investors.

Several prominent global investors participated in the anchor allocation, including Goldman Sachs, Ashoka WhiteOak ICAV, Societe Generale, BofA Securities Europe and Integrated Core Strategies.

Domestic mutual funds also accounted for a significant portion of the anchor placement. Arcil allotted 81.29 lakh shares to 12 schemes managed by six fund houses — White Oak Capital, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC, Bandhan Mutual Fund, Tata Mutual Fund, JM Financial Mutual Fund and Groww Mutual Fund.

Since the issue is an OFS, the IPO proceeds, after deducting issue-related expenses, will accrue to the selling shareholders. These include Avenue India Resurgence, State Bank of India, Lathe Investment, owned by Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC, and Federal Bank.

Arcil reported revenue of Rs 753 crore for the financial year ended March 2026, marking a 26.3 percent increase from Rs 596.4 crore in the previous year. Profit for the year rose 14.8 percent to Rs 407.8 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 355.3 crore in FY25.

Check IPO News Here

IIFL Capital Services, IDBI Capital Markets &amp; Securities and JM Financial are the merchant bankers handling the IPO.

About Asset Reconstruction Company India (Arcil)

Established in August 2003, Arcil was the first asset reconstruction company incorporated in India. It acquires stressed assets from banks and financial institutions and works on their resolution through measures such as restructuring, enforcement of security rights and settlements. The company aims to maximise recoveries from stressed assets while improving the value of the underlying assets.

1.headline: Steamhouse India IPO subscribed 90% so far on Day 2; GMP at 25%
1.heading: Steamhouse India IPO subscribed 90% so far on Day 2; GMP at 25%
1.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of industrial gas supplier Steamhouse India saw a pick-up in demand on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 90 percent subscription as of 12:20 pm on September 10, according to NSE data.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of industrial gas supplier Steamhouse India saw a pick-up in demand on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 90 percent subscription as of 12:20 pm on September 10, according to NSE data.

The Rs 414-crore IPO received bids for 3,36,45,395 shares against 3,76,36,363 shares on offer. The retail investor portion was subscribed 1.45 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category saw 79 percent subscription.

In the grey market, Steamhouse India shares were commanding a premium of 25 percent on September 10, according to InvestorGain. The grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee the company's listing price or returns.

Read Also: Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions IPO subscribed 22% so far on Day 2; check latest GMP

The IPO opened for public subscription on September 9 and will close on September 11. The Rs 414-crore IPO has a price band of Rs 77-81 per share. The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 353 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of shares worth Rs 61 crore by promoter Vishal Sanwarprasad Budhia.

Ahead of the IPO, Steamhouse India raised Rs 124.2 crore from six anchor investors. The company allotted 1.53 crore equity shares to anchor investors at the upper end of the price band.

Singularity Large Value Fund III, managed by Madhusudan Kela-mentored Singularity AMC, and Kela-backed Chartered Finance &amp; Leasing were the largest anchor investors. Each acquired 51.97 lakh shares for Rs 42.09 crore.

Abakkus Emerging Opportunities Fund-1, managed by Sunil Singhania's Abakkus Asset Manager, and Emerge Capital Opportunities Scheme, managed by Emerge Capital, each purchased 12.34 lakh shares for Rs 10 crore.

Niveshaay Sambhav Fund, managed by Arvind Kothari-owned Niveshaay Investment Advisors, acquired 18.51 lakh shares for Rs 15 crore, while 31 Degrees North Fund bought 6.17 lakh shares for Rs 5 crore.

Steamhouse India plans to use Rs 180 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue to repay debt.

Check IPO News Here

Another Rs 75.9 crore has been earmarked for capacity expansion at its Ankleshwar and Panoli facilities. The funds will also support capital expenditure for a new steam-generation manufacturing facility at Dahej GIDC. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Equirus Capital is the merchant banker handling the IPO.

About Steamhouse India

Steamhouse India specialises in generating and centrally distributing industrial gases, including steam and nitrogen, through pipeline networks. The company says it is the only player in India supplying nitrogen through a distributed pipeline network, rather than through cryogenic tanks or on-site nitrogen generation.

2.headline: Manipal Payment & Identity Solutions IPO subscribed 22% so far on Day 2; check latest GMP
2.heading: Manipal Payment & Identity Solutions IPO subscribed 22% so far on Day 2; check latest GMP
2.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Manipal Payment & Identity Solutions continued to witness weak investor interest on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 22 percent subscription as of 11:50 am on September 10, as per the NSE data.
2.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions continued to witness weak investor interest on the second day of bidding, with the issue receiving 22 percent subscription as of 11:50 am on September 10, as per the NSE data.

The Rs 805-crore IPO received bids for 29,05,540 shares against 1,30,60,472 shares on offer. The retail investor portion was subscribed 95 percent, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category received subscription of 18 percent. Bidding for the IPO will remain open until September 11.

The grey market premium (GMP) for Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions stood at zero on September 10, indicating a flat listing, according to Investorgain. The GMP is an unofficial indicator of market sentiment and does not guarantee the listing price or returns.

Read Also: Glass Wall Systems IPO: Issue subscribed over 14x so far on Day 3; GMP signals 36% listing gains

The Rs 805-crore IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs 320 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of shares worth up to Rs 485 crore by promoter Manipal Technologies.

The company has fixed the price band at Rs 322-339 per share. At the upper end of the price band, the fresh issue is expected to raise Rs 320 crore.

Ahead of the IPO, the company raised Rs 362.25 crore from 23 anchor investors. On September 8, Manipal Payment allocated 1.06 crore equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 339 apiece.

Among the anchor investors, 35.1 lakh shares were subscribed by 16 schemes across four domestic mutual fund houses — Motilal Oswal AMC, Baroda BNP Paribas Mutual Fund, ITI Mutual Fund and Groww Mutual Fund.

Edelweiss Life Insurance Company invested Rs 10.01 crore for 2.95 lakh shares, while Abakkus Asset Manager, founded by Sunil Singhania, invested Rs 40 crore.

The company plans to deploy Rs 238.4 crore from the fresh issue towards purchasing and setting up new and second-hand equipment at various facilities.

These include its card manufacturing facility, personalisation bureau and cheque printing facility, central card processing centres, and Smart Tagging and IoT Solutions facility. The remaining funds will be allocated towards general corporate purposes.

Check IPO News Here

Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Axis Capital, ICICI Securities, IIFL Capital Services and Nuvama Wealth Management are the merchant bankers to the issue.

About Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions

Incorporated in 2008, Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions is part of the Manipal Group and provides payment, identification, secure solutions, smart tagging and Internet of Things (IoT) solutions. Its customers include banks, fintech companies, non-banking financial companies and government entities across India and international markets.
